current.Problems__c:

3. Integration friction: Evaluate the new API-first QuickBooks integration against their workflow and use Rev.io’s API and webhooks.

- Billing accuracy: Est. $7K/yr (156 hrs) fixing ~5 broken tickets a month and verifying a 5-step close.
- Margin erosion: Est. $6K/yr lost quoting on prices refreshed only every ~3 months.
- Support time: Est. $3K/yr in weekly PSA support calls, plus 30+ min waits for payments help.
- Client experience: All ~22 products on an invoice show the billing date, not the date used.
current.Solutions__c:
- Mobile app with UPC scanning, timers, offline caching and geofencing to capture labor and parts on site.
- PSA and telecom billing on one database, so tickets and usage flow into one automated invoice run.
- Native quoting from the live price book with real-time distributor pricing.
- SureTax embedded in billing applies the right telecom or sales tax code to every product.
- One platform for PSA, billing, tax and payments with one in-house, US-based support team.
- Full audit log shows who added each product and when it was applied.
current.Values__c: Rev.io recovers an estimated $37.8K-$39.6K per year for Nored, led by about $19.8K in billable labor captured on site and $7K in billing rework eliminated, by running PSA, quoting, telecom billing and tax on one database.

current.Business_Issue_Details__c: Slice Wireless Solutions (about 10 staff, New York) runs Autotask for CRM, quoting and service, with QuickBooks Desktop and spreadsheets on the side. Autotask never integrated with QuickBooks, so installs and upgrades get relayed to billing by message and sometimes go unbilled. current.Problems__c:

- Autotask never integrated with QuickBooks Desktop, so billing is manual; "the big issue really is QuickBooks"
- Service upgrades (50 to 100 meg, $50 to $100 more a month) don't flow back to billing, "a few times a quarter"

- Recurring services and agreements drive billing, so a service upgrade (50 to 100 meg) is picked up from the work instead of relayed to the office
- Mobile app gives techs timers, parts, photos and signature capture, so install time reaches the invoice and the CFO gets profitability
- Projects carry phases and budgeted hours for larger installs

current.Business_Issue_Details__c: Click Computers needs a more suitable way to manage its MSP and repair-shop operations. Odoo, introduced after Tyler Andrews acquired the business, is creating friction across billing, quoting, ticketing, and customer service. Billing is Tyler’s primary complaint.
current.Business_Issues__c: Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor
current.Problems__c:
- Billing and taxes: Adding product line items can disrupt tax calculations, forcing staff to use a generic hardware item and manually edit descriptions and prices.
- Ticket-to-billing workflow: Staff must create a project between the ticket and billing, making work and notes difficult to find.
- Manual administration: Staff check payments daily, follow up on failed payment tokens, and handle some payments by check.
- Slow quoting: Quotes are entered manually; Dalton said a simple monitor order can take about 30 minutes.
- Disconnected systems: Dalton built a one-way NinjaOne-to-Odoo alert integration that he describes as inefficient. The team also uses IT Glue and wants to explore consolidation.
current.Solutions__c:
-Demonstrate billing for recurring services, hardware, and break-fix work, including a new product line item and tax calculation.
-Show how labor, parts, expenses, and agreement entitlements connect to a ticket, and how a purchase order can be created from it.
-Demonstrate a storefront break-fix ticket and mobile payment workflow; validate the team’s specific point-of-sale requirements.
-Review the NinjaOne integration and confirm it meets their alert and ticket workflow.
-Show the Knowledge Hub and provide a feature comparison with IT Glue. Full feature parity was not claimed on the call.
current.Values__c:
- Ticket assignment: 6 hours/week × 4 weeks × $40/hour = $960 per four-week period.
- Tax setup: 1 hour/week × 4 weeks × $40/hour = $160 per four-week period.
- Combined: 28 hours and $1,120 per four-week period, subject to validating that the activities do not overlap.
- Odoo: approximately $1,000/month in reported cost; the amount Click can actually eliminate is unconfirmed.
- Quote configuration: 25–50 quotes/week at 15 minutes each represents 6.25–12.5 hours/week. Some quotes take 30 minutes. Quote time is excluded from the ROI model until the average duration, potential improvement and overlap with tax setup are verified.
current.Risk_Mitigation_Plan__c:
Existing Odoo investment: Tyler uses Odoo for PoE Texas, and Click Computers runs a second instance. Confirm whether the MSP can move independently and what costs would remain.
Unproven ROI: Quantify actual activity and costs before presenting a financial case.
